_comment: Seed fixture for the source-code-analysis-htmx widget-type bead.
Created for ka-0000006619 (free-htmx port — sixth port after
activity-log-htmx, MR !2334 / ka-0000004584; related-tickets-htmx,
MR !2346 / ka-0000005540; header-incident-summary-htmx, MR !2347 /
ka-0000005304; reproduction-steps-htmx, MR !2350 / ka-0000007835;
reporter-info-htmx, ka-0000004065; event-timeline-htmx,
ka-0000000243; ai-recommended-actions-htmx, ka-0000000272). This is
the FIRST Phase-5 port — source-code-analysis is a code-highlighted
widget (widgets_phase5.go) so the parity gap surface is wider than
the Phase-4 ports. Strategy A — port-then-soak: lives alongside the
Go-coded `source-code-analysis` slug rather than replacing it.
Authoring path:
kd create 'Free-htmx widget: source-code-analysis-htmx' \
--type=widget-type \
-F gardenio/controller/cmd/beads-viewer/fixtures/source-code-analysis-htmx.json
Pre-write hooks (kbeads/internal/server/widget_validation.go) parse
template_source under html/template and reject malformed inputs at
createBead/updateBead time, so a bad fixture surfaces immediately.
Schema validation runs against widget-instance writes per the same
pre-write hook; the schema below is the wire contract.
The wire contract mirrors the Go-coded `source-code-analysis`
renderer at widgets_phase5.go::renderSourceCodeAnalysis —
findings[] of {path, line, function, severity, headline, detail,
language, code}. Three intentional parity gaps vs. the Go path,
all documented in TestSourceCodeAnalysisParity:
1. Chroma syntax highlighting. The Go path runs each finding's
`code` field through the shared codeHighlighter (chroma,
github-dark theme, server-side, cached). The htmx template
body has no Go-side hook into chroma, so the rendered <pre>
carries plain escaped text rather than chroma's token spans.
Producers cutting a source-code-analysis-htmx widget-instance
get readable code without the colourised tokens; the existing
CSS `.ii-w-sca-code` chrome still applies.
2. Severity normalisation. The Go path lower-cases the severity
string before emitting `data-state="…"`. The htmx template
renders the field verbatim, so producers MUST emit severity
as a pre-lower-cased string (`"error"` / `"warn"` / `"info"`)
for the Phase-1 state-pill CSS to match.
3. Jump-to-IDE buttons. The Go renderer emits one
`<button class="ii-action-btn">` per finding that carries a
`path` (built via OpenIDEAction). The htmx template body cannot
reach that helper, so the optional jump-to-line field is
silently ignored. Same gap as ai-recommended-actions-htmx /
header-incident-summary-htmx; blocks on a future template-side
button-builder fn (research ka-0000002102 §3.3).

fields.template_source:
{{- $title := index .Payload "title" -}} {{- $findings := index .Payload "findings" -}} {{if $title}}

{{$title}}

{{end}} {{if $findings}}
    {{range $findings}}
  1. {{if .severity}}{{.severity}}{{end}} {{.path}}{{if .line}}:{{.line}}{{end}} {{if .function}}in {{.function}}(){{end}}
    {{if .headline}}

    {{.headline}}

    {{end}} {{if .detail}}

    {{.detail}}

    {{end}} {{if .code}}
    {{.code}}
    {{end}}
    2. {{end}}
{{else}}

No source-code findings.

{{end}}
